Hi Pedro —

Thanks for the heads up and for attaching the remittance. Quick answers up front: we can accept EUR to our EU billing entity (preferred) OR USD to our US entity; intermediary fees are typically charged by the sender's bank / correspondent chain unless the instruction uses OUR.

A couple of clarifying items so we give the right bank details:
- Which legal entity is on the invoice (Redwood Inference Inc vs Redwood Inference Ltd)?
- Please share your VAT number for reverse-charge validation.

Laura from finance is best placed to provide the EU IBAN and confirm the policy on fee recovery — looping her in. I’ll propose options: (A) pay EUR to EU IBAN (no correspondent expected), (B) send to US and request OUR (sender) to cover fees, or (C) pay EUR and we credit any proven intermediary fee up to a one-time cap.

We aim to confirm before your Monday run.

Appreciate the quick follow-up. We’ll make this straightforward:

- Primary ask: please attempt payment to the EU IBAN exactly as provided. If your bank can set charges to OUR, that avoids deductions.
- Contingency: if intermediary fees are deducted (SHA), Redwood will credit back proven intermediary fees up to €25 one-time for this invoice. Please send the SWIFT trace (MT103 or equivalent) to treasury@redwood.com after the payment posts and we will process the credit on the next billing cycle.
- VAT: we accept reverse-charge for EU B2B when the invoice is billed to our EU entity. We’ve captured your VAT ID DE123456789 and confirm our VAT ID GB987654321 — please keep the billing address aligned with your VAT registration.

Next steps:
1) Pedro / Elaine — confirm which bank (Frankfurt / London) will originate the payment and whether they can set OUR.
2) If you proceed and a deduction occurs, forward the MT103 to treasury@redwood.com for the one-time credit.
3) If you prefer, we can send a short amendment via DocuSign to note the credit policy for this invoice — let me know and I’ll route it to you.

Happy to escalate if your bank still rejects OUR.
